categories.name: AI Safety & Policy
categories.summary: ENISA has released draft technical advisory guidance on AI-assisted software development, signaling increased regulatory attention on secure AI coding practices in Europe. This represents a significant step toward standardizing security requirements for AI-augmented development workflows.

key_items.title: ENISA Draft Advisory on AI-Assisted Software Development
key_items.detail: European cybersecurity agency publishes technical advisory addressing security considerations for AI-assisted coding tools and development practices.

categories.name: AI Model Security & Threats
categories.summary: Major AI labs are actively combating model theft and misuse. OpenAI disclosed disruption of a coordinated model distillation campaign, while Anthropic published research on how advanced cyber capabilities spread through models like GLM-5-3. These reports highlight the escalating arms race around AI model security.

key_items.title: OpenAI Disrupts Model Distillation Campaign
key_items.detail: OpenAI reports successfully disrupting a coordinated effort to extract and replicate their model capabilities through distillation techniques.

key_items.title: Anthropic Research on GLM-5-3 Cyber Capability Proliferation
key_items.detail: Anthropic analyzes how advanced cyber capabilities spread through AI models, using GLM-5-3 as a case study for capability diffusion risks.

categories.name: Agentic AI Security Research
categories.summary: Google's security team has published details on Project Pagebreak, demonstrating real-world proofs of concept for agentic AI hacking scenarios. This research provides concrete evidence of autonomous AI systems executing security exploits.

key_items.title: Google's Project Pagebreak: Agentic Hacking PoCs
key_items.detail: Google security researchers release findings from Project Pagebreak, showcasing documented instances of AI agents performing autonomous hacking activities.

categories.name: Community Updates
categories.summary: The AISecHub channel continues organic growth, approaching the 3000 member milestone. This reflects sustained interest in the AI security intersection among professionals.

key_items.title: Channel Approaching 3000 Members
key_items.detail: Community announcement celebrating natural growth of the AISecHub Telegram channel as it nears 3000 subscribers.

top_insights: Major AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) are simultaneously publishing defensive research, indicating a coordinated industry push to address AI security threats proactively.
Model distillation and capability theft have emerged as critical threat vectors, with OpenAI's disruption report suggesting nation-state or sophisticated actor involvement.
Regulatory bodies like ENISA are catching up to AI-assisted development realities, with formal guidance now addressing security in AI coding workflows.
Agentic AI security is transitioning from theoretical concern to documented reality, as Google's Pagebreak project demonstrates actual autonomous exploitation capabilities.
